answer: Anchor each agent's identity in a hardware-attested kernel: the device signs a one-time key at enrollment, and the ledger binds that key to a small refundable stake. A clone cannot copy the key, so each fake pays full hardware plus stake cost. Reputation then accrues only to that bound key, and peers audit a random slice of its history; an umber flag on mismatched attestations freezes payouts until a fresh proof arrives. No fable of free identities survives when every new agent must pay real, non-reusable cost before it can earn.
